title: Peripheral sensory neurons clock genes are a molecular driver of pain rhythmicity
title_zh: 外周感觉神经元时钟基因是疼痛节律性的分子驱动因素
abstract: Abstract Pain intensity fluctuates across the day in patients, yet the cellular clock mechanisms that generate pain rhythmicity and their therapeutic potential remain poorly defined. Prior studies have established circadian variation in nociception and a requirement for intact clock function, but it has remained unclear the neurophysiological mechanisms which translate clock state into time-of-day changes in pain. The goal of this study was to define the clock component(s) and effector pathway(s) that drive pain rhythmicity and to test whether this axis can be exploited for analgesia. We combined behavioural analyses under circadian conditions with genetic dissection of clock components in sensory neurons, electrophysiological interrogation of nociceptor excitability, and pharmacological modulation of the clock machinery. To establish translational relevance, we used human iPSC-derived nociceptors, including a human pain disease model, to test whether the same clock–excitability coupling operates in human cells. We show that nociceptive behaviours exhibit robust circadian rhythmicity and that this rhythmicity depends on the molecular clock within peripheral sensory neurons. Loss of cryptochromes CRY1/CRY2 disrupts time-of-day differences in nociceptor excitability, identifying cryptochromes as essential clock effectors in the pain pathway. Mechanistically, cryptochrome state controls voltage-gated sodium channel function, providing a direct link from clock machinery to nociceptor responsiveness. Pharmacological stabilisation of cryptochromes using a small-molecule modulator suppresses sodium currents and reduces nociceptive responses across distinct pain paradigms, and this effect is abrogated when cryptochrome function is absent. In synchronised human iPSC-derived nociceptors, we observe concordant clock-state-dependent changes in excitability, and cryptochrome stabilisation reduces hyperexcitability. These findings identify a peripheral sensory neuron clock mechanism that drives pain rhythmicity through cryptochrome-dependent control of sodium channel function and highlight cryptochrome stabilisation as a non-opioid therapeutic strategy for pain disorders with diurnal symptom variation.
abstract_zh: 摘要：患者的疼痛强度在一天中会波动，但产生疼痛节律性的细胞钟机制及其治疗潜力尚未明晰。先前研究已证实痛觉存在昼夜变化，并需要完整的时钟功能，但尚不清楚将时钟状态转化为疼痛时间变化的神经生理机制。本文旨在确定驱动疼痛节律性的时钟组分及其效应通路，并检验该轴是否可用于镇痛。我们将昼夜条件下的行为分析与感觉神经元时钟组分的遗传剖析、痛觉受体兴奋性电生理检测以及时钟机制的药理调节相结合。为验证转化意义，我们使用人类诱导多能干细胞（iPSC）衍生的痛觉受体，包括人类疼痛疾病模型，检验相同的时钟–兴奋性耦合是否在人体细胞中存在。结果显示，痛觉行为表现出强烈的昼夜节律性，且该节律性依赖于外周感觉神经元内的分子时钟。缺失暗色素CRY1/CRY2会破坏痛觉受体兴奋性在不同时间的差异，表明暗色素是疼痛通路中必需的时钟效应器。机制上，暗色素状态调控电压门控钠通道功能，直接将时钟机制与痛觉受体响应性相连。使用小分子调节剂稳定暗色素可抑制钠电流并降低多种疼痛模型中的痛觉反应，而当暗色素功能缺失时，该效应被消除。在同步的人类iPSC衍生痛觉受体中，我们观察到与时钟状态相关的兴奋性变化一致，暗色素稳定化可降低过度兴奋性。这些发现揭示了外周感觉神经元时钟机制通过暗色素依赖的钠通道功能控制来驱动疼痛节律性，并强调暗色素稳定化作为一种非阿片类治疗策略，用于昼夜症状变化的疼痛疾病。
